clues.fortune_text: Where butter is kept, look one jar to the right: there the flour sits waiting, powdery white.
clues.nudge: Read past the rhyme. The couplet names two ingredients and a direction: start at the first one's jar and move the way it says.

clues.fortune_text: Penguin dads keep the egg close all winter. So does sugar: the egg sits one jar left of sugar.
clues.nudge: The penguin is only a picture. The second sentence is the instruction: it names two ingredients and which side of one the other is on.

clues.fortune_text: Which version of the GNU GPL came out in 1989? Butter goes in the jar with that number.
clues.nudge: Look up when each version of the GNU General Public License was published. The version number is a jar number.

clues.fortune_text: On a jar lid, in the gnu's ROT13: Fhtne vf va wne svir.
clues.nudge: ROT13 swaps every letter with the one 13 places along the alphabet: A and N swap, B and O swap, and so on. Swap each letter of the scrambled words.

clues.fortune_text: assert jar["flour"] == jar["vanilla"] - 1  # jar 1 is on the left
clues.nudge: jar["x"] means the number of the jar that holds x. An assert is a line that must be true, so read it as plain arithmetic about two jar numbers.

clues.fortune_text: Wire the jars like a pin header, pin 1 on the left: vanilla's pin is just left of egg's pin.
clues.nudge: The pins on a header sit in one row, numbered in order, so a pin's neighbours are one number lower and one higher. Here each pin number is a jar number.
